# Chapter Two

The bridge was gone and the river had not noticed. Mara had green eyes, and she crossed at the ford counting the doors of the village as she always did.

The Harrow road, which the flood of 1889 had taken, was where the sacks had gone. Teodor's ledger — the Book of Hours, he called it, though it was only flour — lay open at the mill.

He had kept that ledger for eleven years. She thought of her grandmother's honey, sold in pickle jars with labels in her own hand; the old woman had never written anything else down.
